open.speaker: earl
lines: Two fellas in black suits came by Tuesday. Asked which folks saw the bird. Asked about the bridge too.
Paid in bills so new they stuck together. Car had no plates. Smiled like they'd read about smiling.

passives.line: He said don't look. So you don't. Good. Hands on the counter, eyes on Earl, and breathe like you mean it.
He isn't afraid of them. He is afraid of being the one in town who talked about them.
'Smiled like they'd read about smiling.' You have read that sentence before, in an older book, about a thing that was not a man either.

static.line: Look at the pumps. Go on. They want you to look, and you want to. What's the harm in looking?

options.text: Take your time, Earl. We're just buying gas.
We're with them. We're checking your story matches.

gas.speaker: earl
lines: Seven dollars on pump two. Yeah. Yeah, that's fine.
They asked about a woman, too. Not the bird. A woman from Sutton, from way back, like I'd know. I was nine in '67.
Why's everybody from Sutton this month.
Because she never came home, Earl. And we are the ones who still keep her desk.

passives.line: Sutton. 1967. The Office's founder was in this town the week the bridge fell. The suits asked about her before they asked about you.

car.speaker: earl
lines: Black Ford. Galaxie, near enough, but a Galaxie that nobody's dealer ever sold. Clean. February and not a speck of salt on it.
Saw it again Wednesday, after midnight. Parked at the Riverview, nose out, lights off, engine running. Nobody in it. Engine running.
Nose out. Lights off. That's a car that's waiting for somebody to come out of a room.

passives.line: No salt on a car in February means it has not been on a road in February. You do not know where it has been instead.

car_fail.speaker: earl
lines: Don't know cars. I pump 'em, I don't read 'em.
Kid on the courthouse corner knows every car in this county by the sound. Ask him what parks at the motel after midnight. Don't say I sent you.

bluff_pass.speaker: earl
lines: ...Oh. Oh, Lord. I told 'em everything, I swear, I told 'em Marlene and the deputy and the reverend, same as I'll tell you.
They gave me a number. Charleston exchange. Said to call if anybody came asking about them. I ain't called. I'll call now if you want, I'll call right now.
Stop. Earl, stop. We're not them. I'm sorry. We're not them.

passives.line: You did that to him. It worked. Now you know what the suits told him to do, and he will never pour your coffee the same way.

bluff_fail.speaker: earl
lines: With them. Sure. Then you know what I told 'em.
Told 'em what the paper said. Big grey crane, off its path, red head. That's what I saw in '66 and that's what I told your friends and I'll tell it to anybody.
He's reciting. We just taught him we're not worth the real one.

passives.line: He gave you the crane because the crane is the safe answer, the one that was printed. You walked out with the official story and called it a lead.

silent.speaker: earl
lines: They're gone. They go. They come back Tuesdays, like the bread truck.
You're the first ones who didn't look. The reverend looked. Looked right at 'em and then went to bed for two days.

passives.line: You held. Two minutes with your back to an empty forecourt and you held. That is the whole job, some days.

hub.speaker: earl
lines: Need anything else? Wipers, map, somebody to tell you it's all nothing?

options.text: (Pay for the gas, and leave a twenty on the counter for his time.)
(Turn around and look at the pumps.)

paid.speaker: earl
lines: ...I'll keep it. You want, I'll call Sutton if that car comes through again. I got the number off your wagon. I notice things. I just don't look at 'em.
That's the most useful twenty we'll spend in this town.

look.speaker: earl
lines: ...Huh. Nobody. Just the Ford pulling out onto 62. North. Towards the plant.
He waved. Did you see him wave? He had a hat on. Nobody wears a hat.
No plates. Going north. He got here before us.

passives.line: You looked, and it was only a car, and the car was only leaving. Your hands are fine. Your hands are absolutely fine.
A tired man in a hat, older than his car, polite. He was not here for the gas and he did not come for Earl.

look_fail.speaker: earl
lines: Why'd you look. You looked and now he's seen you look. Get out. Get your gas somewhere else, get it in Gallipolis.

passives.line: There was a man at pump two. He raised one hand, friendly, the way you would. You cannot say, afterward, what his face was, and you will try all night.

static.line: He looked like you. That's why Earl's shouting. He looked exactly like you.
